Rashi on Shabbat 56a:10:1.english: With the sword of the children of Ammon - Like those whom the children of Ammon kill without your knowledge.

Rashi on Shabbat 56a:11:1.english: And my lord Joab - It is not proper conduct to accept the authority of others upon oneself in the presence of the king.

Rashi on Shabbat 56a:12:1.hebrew: רק בדבר אוריה - מקרא כתיב כך: בדבר אוריה — שגרם לו שיהרג, אבל בבת שבע לא חטא:
Rashi on Shabbat 56a:12:1.english: Save only in the matter of Uriah - The verse is written thus: "In the matter of Uriah" — [meaning] that he caused him to be killed, but regarding Bathsheba, he did not sin.

Rashi on Shabbat 56a:14:1.hebrew: בלא דבר - אינו חכם בתורה, והוא מצאו מלא דבר וחכם בתורה:
Rashi on Shabbat 56a:14:1.english: In Lo-Devar [belo devar] - [Meaning that] he is not wise in Torah; but he [David] found him full of matter and wise in Torah.

Rashi on Shabbat 56a:15:1.english: He saw that he was a liar - Initially, he found him to be a liar in this [regard].

Rashi on Shabbat 56a:15:2.hebrew: כי הדר אלשין עליה - ציבא על מפיבושת, כשהיה דוד בורח מפני אבשלום — מאי טעמא קביל מיניה:
Rashi on Shabbat 56a:15:2.english: When he slandered him again - [Namely,] Ziba against Mephibosheth, when David was fleeing from Absalom — what was the reason [David] accepted [it] from him?

Rashi on Shabbat 56a:15:3.english: “Where is your master’s son? And he said: Behold, he is staying in Jerusalem” - [The verse continues:] “For he said: Today they will restore to me the kingdom of my father.”

Rashi on Shabbat 56a:16:1.hebrew: דברים הנכרים חזא ביה - במפיבושת: כשנהרג אבשלום וחזר דוד למלכותו ובא לפניו, לא עשה רגליו ולא עשה שפמו. כסבור דוד שניכרים דברי ציבא — שנצטער על שחזר דוד, ולא קישט עצמו, ועוד היה מצפה שכשיושיבוהו במלכות יתנאה ויסתפר. לכך לא קבל דבריו, ואמר לו: אתה וציבא תחלקו השדה. והוא השיבו קשה: אין לי לצעוק אלא על מי שהביאך הלום — הנה שמצטער על שובו! ואם לא שראה בו דברים הניכרים, היה חוזר ממה שאמר: הנה לך כל אשר למפיבושת. ואע"פ שמיהר ואמר לו מתחלה: הנה לך כל אשר למפיבושת — אין זו קבלה, כי כל זמן שלא היה דוד שב למלכותו יודע היה שאין מתנתו מתנה, ולא אמר לו אלא על תנאי: אם יראה אמת בדבריו:
Rashi on Shabbat 56a:16:1.english: He saw conspicuous matters in him - In Mephibosheth: When Absalom was killed and David returned to his kingship, and [Mephibosheth] came before him, he had not dressed his feet and had not trimmed his beard. David thought that Ziba's words were substantiated — that [Mephibosheth] was distressed that David had returned, and [therefore] had not groomed himself; and moreover, he had been anticipating that when they would install him in the kingship, he would adorn himself and cut his hair. Therefore, he did not accept his words, and said to him: 'You and Ziba shall divide the estate.' And he answered him harshly: 'I have no grievance except against the One Who brought you here' — behold, this demonstrates that he was distressed over his return! And had he not seen conspicuous matters in him, he would have retracted what he said: 'Behold, all that belongs to Mephibosheth is yours.' And even though he was hasty and said to him initially: 'Behold, all that belongs to Mephibosheth is yours,' this was not an acceptance [of slander], because as long as David had not returned to his kingship, he knew that his gift was not a [valid] gift, and he said it to him only conditionally: if he would see truth in his words.

Rashi on Shabbat 56a:1:1.english: The sons of Samuel sinned - By taking bribes and perverting justice.

Rashi on Shabbat 56a:2:1.hebrew: לחזניהם - שמשיהם, ששוכרין אותן לילך ולהזמין את הנקראים לדין:
Rashi on Shabbat 56a:2:1.english: To their attendants - Their attendants, whom they hire to go and summon those called to judgment:

Rashi on Shabbat 56a:2:2.english: And to their scribes - For deeds of arbitration and for documents of appraisal.

Rashi on Shabbat 56a:3:1.hebrew: חלקם שאלו בפיהם - מעשר ראשון הראוי להם — שלוים היו — שאלו בפיהם. מתוך שהיו גדולי הדור ושופטים, לא היו מונעים מהם, ושאר לוים עניים מצטערים. ולר' מאיר, לא חטאו בהטיית משפט:
Rashi on Shabbat 56a:3:1.english: They vocally demanded their portions - [Namely,] the first tithe that was due to them — for they were Levites — they demanded with their mouth. Since they were the leaders of the generation and judges, [people] would not withhold [it] from them, and the other, poor Levites suffered. And according to Rabbi Meir, they did not sin by perverting justice.

Rashi on Shabbat 56a:3:2.hebrew: מלאי הטילו על בעלי בתים - נותנים להן פרגמטיא לעסוק בה ולתת להם השכר, ומתוך כך היה נמשך לבם להטות דין כשבאין לפניהן לדון, והיינו חטאם:
Rashi on Shabbat 56a:3:2.english: They imposed merchandise upon homeowners - [They would] give them merchandise to trade with and to give them the profit, and because of this their hearts were drawn to pervert justice when they came before them to be judged, and that was their sin.

Rashi on Shabbat 56a:3:3.english: An extra basket - More than what was due.

Rashi on Shabbat 56a:3:4.hebrew: מתנות - זרוע, לחיים וקיבה, והם לא היו כהנים. ל"א: מתנות לויה, כגון מעשר. וקרא כתיב: "ונתן לכהן", ודרשינן: "ולא שיטול מעצמו" בשחיטת חולין, בפ' הזרוע (חולין דף קלג.) — וה"ה לכל מתנות כהונה ולויה:
Rashi on Shabbat 56a:3:4.english: Gifts - [The] foreleg, the cheeks, and the abomasum — and they were not priests. Another explanation: Gifts of the Levites, such as tithe; and the verse states: “And he shall give to the priest,” and we expound: “and not that he may take [it] himself,” in [tractate] Shechitat Chullin, in the chapter [entitled] Hazero'a (Chullin 133a) — and the same applies to all priestly and Levitical gifts.

Rashi on Shabbat 56a:4:1.english: David sinned - With Bathsheba, before she received a bill of divorce.

Rashi on Shabbat 56a:5:1.hebrew: שבקש - לשכב עמה קודם שקבלה גט שהיה בעלה שולח לה מן המלחמה, שאם ימות לא תיזקק ליבום, או שמא יהרג ואין מעיד עליו ותתעגן אשתו, או שמא יהא שבוי — כדאמרינן לקמן: ״כל היוצא למלחמת בית דוד כו'״:
Rashi on Shabbat 56a:5:1.english: That he sought - to lie with her before she received the bill of divorce that her husband was sending to her from the war — so that if he died she would not be subject to levirate marriage, or lest he be killed and there be no one to testify about him and his wife would be bound [as an agunah], or lest he be taken captive — as we say later: “Anyone who goes out to the war of the House of David...”

Rashi on Shabbat 56a:6:1.english: This evil is different - In its writing and in its phrasing:

Rashi on Shabbat 56a:7:1.hebrew: שהיה לך לדונו - על שמרד במלכות, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Shabbat 56a:7:1.english: That you should have judged him - For rebelling against the monarchy, as [explained] below.

Rashi on Shabbat 56a:7:2.hebrew: ליקוחין יש לך בה - קדושין תופסין בה, שאינה אשת איש, כדשמואל כו':
Rashi on Shabbat 56a:7:2.english: You have marriage rights with her - Betrothal takes effect upon her, for she is not a married woman, in accordance with [Rabbi] Shmuel, etc.

Rashi on Shabbat 56a:8:1.hebrew: גט כריתות - על תנאי, שאם ימות תהא מגורשת מעכשיו. ופעמים שהוא טרוד בצאתו, ושולחו מן המלחמה:
Rashi on Shabbat 56a:8:1.english: A bill of divorce - [It was given] on condition that if he dies, she will be divorced [retroactively] from now. And sometimes he is preoccupied upon his departure, and [so] sends it from the war.

Rashi on Shabbat 56a:8:2.english: And take their pledge - [This verse] is written concerning the war of Saul:

Rashi on Shabbat 56a:9:1.hebrew: דברים המעורבים ביניהם - היינו קדושין. "תקח" — תבטל ע"י גט שתביא להם מן המלחמה:
Rashi on Shabbat 56a:9:1.english: Matters that are shared between them - That is, betrothal. “You shall take” — you shall nullify [them] by means of a bill of divorce that you will bring for them from the war.

Tosafot on Shabbat 56a:11:1.hebrew: דאמר ליה ואדוני יואב - פרש"י, דמורד במלכות הוה משום דקאמר "ואדוני יואב". ואין נראה, דאין זה מורד, שלא היה בלבו להמליכו ולקרותו מלך; אלא כמו שפירש רבינו מאיר, דהוי מורד משום דבסיפא דקרא כתיב: "ואני אבא אל ביתי לאכול ולשתות ולשכב עם אשתי וגו'", שדוד אמר לו לעשות, ולא רצה לעשות:
Tosafot on Shabbat 56a:11:1.english: "As he said to him: 'And my lord Joab'" - Rashi explained that he was a rebel against the monarchy because he said "and my lord Joab" [in the presence of the king]. But this does not seem [correct], for this is not [the act of] a rebel, as it was not in his heart to make him king or to call him king. Rather, [it is] as Rabbeinu Meir explained: that he was a rebel because at the end of the verse it is written: "And shall I go to my house to eat and to drink and to lie with my wife...?" (II Samuel 11:11) — which David told him to do, yet he did not want to do [it].

Tosafot on Shabbat 56a:12:1.hebrew: רק בדבר אוריה החתי - קשה, דהא איכא מעשה דהסתה בריש פ"ב דיומא (דף כב:). וי"ל, דלא חשיב ליה, דלא הוי כל כך עון גדול, וגם שגג:
Tosafot on Shabbat 56a:12:1.english: "Save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite" - This is difficult, for there is the incident of the incitement [to count the people] at the beginning of chapter 2 of Yoma (22b). And one can say that [the verse] does not count it because it was not such a great sin, and he also acted unwittingly.

Tosafot on Shabbat 56a:7:1.hebrew: שהיה לך לדונו בסנהדרין - קשה לר"י, דפ"ק דמגילה (דף יד: ושם) אמרינן גבי נבל דמורד במלכות לא בעי למדייניה, ואוריה מורד במלכות הוה, כדאמר בסמוך! ויש לומר: דודאי צריך לדונו, ולידע אם הוא מורד במלכות; אבל לעיין בדינו, ולעשות הלנת דין, ולהמתין עד למחר — אין צריך. וכן משמע, דבסנהדרין (דף לו. ושם) אמר שדן דוד את נבל בסנהדרין, מויחגרו איש חרבו וגו':
Tosafot on Shabbat 56a:7:1.english: “That you should have judged him before the Sanhedrin” - The Ri raises a difficulty: For in the first chapter of Megillah (14b and there), we say regarding Nabal that a rebel against the monarchy does not require to be judged, and Uriah was a rebel against the monarchy, as [the Gemara] states nearby! And one can say that he certainly must be judged to determine whether he is a rebel against the monarchy, but to deliberate over his verdict, to carry out an overnight delay of judgment [halanat din], and to wait until tomorrow is not required. And this is also indicated by [the fact] that in Sanhedrin (36a and there), [the Gemara] says that David judged Nabal before the Sanhedrin, [derived] from: “And they girded on each man his sword” etc.

Tosafot on Shabbat 56a:7:2.hebrew: ליקוחין יש לך בה - אף על גב דאפילו חטא נמי יש לו בה ליקוחין, דהא אנוסה היתה ושריא לבעל, וה"ה לבועל — מ"מ "ליקוחין יש לך בה" משמע: לא היה לך בה עבירה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 56a:7:2.english: “You have marriage rights with her” - Even though, even if he had sinned, he would still have marriage rights with her — for she was [acting under] duress and is permitted to [her] husband, and the same applies to the paramour — nevertheless, “you have marriage rights with her” implies that you had no sin with her.

Tosafot on Shabbat 56a:8:1.hebrew: גט כריתות כותב לאשתו - פרש"י: על תנאי שאם ימות במלחמה תהא מגורשת מעכשיו. וצריך לומר לפירושו, דאף על גב דאוריה בא מן המלחמה, התנאי היה שאם לא ישוב בסוף המלחמה שיהא גט. אך קשה, דתנן במי שאחזו (גיטין דף עג. ושם): "מה היא באותן הימים? רבי יהודה אומר: הרי היא כאשת איש לכל דבריה" — ואם כן, לר' יהודה היתה אשת איש גמורה! ונראה לר"ת, שהיה מגרשה לגמרי, בלא שום תנאי. והא דאמרינן בהזהב (ב"מ דף נט. ושם): "מוטב שיבעול אדם ספק אשת איש ואל ילבין פני חבירו ברבים, מנלן? מדוד" — קרי לה "ספק אשת איש" לפי שהיו מגרשים בצנעה, והעולם סבורים שהיא אשת איש:
Tosafot on Shabbat 56a:8:1.english: Writes a bill of divorce to his wife - Rashi explained: [It was given] on condition that if he dies in battle, she will be divorced retroactively from now. And according to his explanation, one must say that even though Uriah returned from the war, the condition was that if he does not return at the end of the war, it should be a bill of divorce. However, this is difficult, for we learned in a mishna in Mi She’aḥazo (Gittin 73a): “What is her status during those days? Rabbi Yehuda says: She is like a married woman in all respects.” And if so, according to Rabbi Yehuda, she was a full-fledged married woman! And it appears to Rabbeinu Tam that he would divorce her completely, without any condition. And as for that which we say in HaZahav (Bava Metzia 59a): “It is better for a person to engage in relations with a possible married woman than to publicly humiliate his fellow; from where do we derive this? From David” — [the Gemara there] calls her a “possible married woman” because they would divorce in secret, and people assumed that she was a married woman.
